title: Docked in the centre, or anchored offshore
subtitle: The single difference that changes every morning of the week.

text: A river ship ties up where the town actually is.
sub: Step off after breakfast, come back for an hour, go out again after dinner. No tender ticket, no coach from an industrial berth.

items.head: Vienna and Budapest
items.body: You are walking, not transferring. The evening ashore is yours as well as the day.

items.head: The Douro's terraced villages
items.body: Small quays a large ship cannot use at all. The vessel is the only sensible way in.

items.head: A wet, grey day
items.body: On a river you go back aboard for an hour and out again. Offshore, that costs you the port.

quote: A river ship doesn't take you near the place. It ties up in it.

text: Ask where the ship berths, not only which ports it lists.
sub: Same town on two itineraries can mean a five-minute walk or a forty-minute coach. The docking plan is the itinerary.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Or tell me the week you have in mind and I'll send back a two-line verdict: river or ocean, and why.
